- Primary goal: Reduce latency on your customer-facing summarization pipeline while preserving invoice-extraction accuracy and reducing hallucinations.
- Current infra: mixture of hosted + some on-prem inference behind a VPC.
- Recommended initial model candidates: redwood/open-llama-7B-quant (fastest), redwood/redwood-2-13B (best quality for extraction).
- Suggested evals: (1) 1k prompt regression run (sampling across invoice templates you sent), (2) precision/recall on key fields, (3) hallucination rate on negative examples.

Attachments: acme-benchmark-diff.csv (sample outputs from our last eval), prompt-sets-v1.txt (shared in Drive link). See full benchmark here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cAcmeBenchmark

Proposed next steps:
1) You share a prioritized prompt set (you mentioned 200 examples to start).
2) We run a focused regression vs your current prod model and the two recommended candidates (ETA 3 business days).
3) If we see degradation, we can pin the serving model version or rollback the recent runtime change — we'll coordinate with your SRE.

Would you like us to start the 1k regression run this week? If yes, please confirm the set of templates and which environment to use (staging vs prod canary).

Marissa

We want to proceed but we have an urgent issue: after your v2.3 runtime rollout last week our production summaries started hallucinating financial line items more often. Example: Prompt ID 47 (invoice template A) used to return "total_due: $1,234.56" but now returns an extra line item "service_fee: $120" that doesn't exist in the source.

We pulled a before/after sample for ~50 invoices and see a ~8% increase in hallucination rate (we attached the sample rows in the HubSpot file). This is blocking our Q2 reporting. Can you look into whether the v2.3 kernel/quant change could have introduced a regression?

We'd prefer a rollback/pinning option if it's quick — staging canary is fine but our timelines are tight. Happy to jump on a screen share if that helps.

Marissa / team — dug into the rollout logs and diffed the runtime changes between v2.2 and v2.3. Preliminary notes: 

- Root cause hypothesis: a tokenization tweak and a default temperature/response-filter change in the v2.3 serving profile increased model verbosity on edge invoice prompts. Additionally, one of the optimized kernels changed byte-level padding which affects the model's alignment on very short structured inputs (invoices). We see the same failure mode on our regression harness for several templates.

- Quick mitigations: 
  1) Pin ACME's org to model runtime v2.2 (we can do a per-org override in the routing layer). This is low-risk and reversible.
  2) Start a targeted canary: Run v2.2 on 10% of ACME traffic (staging first if they prefer) and compare hallucination metrics over 24-48 hours.
  3) Add a prompt-safety post-check for invoice extraction to remove fields not present in source (short-term).

- ETA: We can implement the org-level pin within 2 hours during our maintenance window and deploy the canary within 4-6 hours. Full rollback of the runtime globally would require an ops window and coordination (2-4 hours).

I've attached a short diff and the rollout notes: v2.3-rollout-notes.pdf. Recommend we propose pin+canary to ACME now and plan a controlled rollback only if metrics don't improve.

Dev

Alex / Samira — thanks for raising this and for the sample outputs. Our eng team dug in and we have a recommended remediation plan that we can execute immediately: 

Plan (summary):
1) Pin your org to runtime v2.2 at the routing layer (instant override). We can do this now once you give the go-ahead — no change to your client calls.
2) Launch a 10% canary (staging or prod per your preference) running v2.2 vs v2.3 for 48 hours and compare hallucination/precision metrics.
3) If canary shows expected improvement, keep v2.2 for your org and schedule a follow-up deeper regression to allow model/vendor-level fixes before any global v2.3 re-rollout.
4) Short-term: apply a prompt post-check to filter inferred fields for invoice extraction.

Attachments: rollback-plan-v2.2.docx (outline of steps + rollback runbook). Full benchmark and diff: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cAcmeBenchmark

Tell me if you want us to proceed with the pin now; if yes we'll require a 15-minute window to make the org override and then monitor the canary results, reporting back within 24h.
